dialogue.Introduction: Oh! A new face in Pelican Town. I am the Painter, though most folks around here only know me as the one who trips over her own easel. Pleased to meet you, @.$h
dialogue.Mon: Mornings are for sketching the river mist before it burns off. Monday mist is always the best kind.$h
dialogue.Tue: Tuesday. I meant to paint the forest today but my palette would not behave. Blame the damp.
dialogue.Wed: Have you seen the colors the cliffs turn this time of year? I keep chasing the right orange and I never quite catch it.
dialogue.Thu: My canvases are piling up in the cottage. The Nurse says I am a fire hazard with all the turpentine. She is not wrong.$s
dialogue.Fri: Friday is market day, and the Merchant is charging me double for linseed oil again. Art is not cheap, @.
dialogue.Sat: Saturday. Let me show you what I have been working on. It is not finished, so do not judge it too harshly.$u
dialogue.Sun: Sundays I rest my hands and just walk the forest with my sketchbook. The trees here are the best models in the valley.$h
dialogue.Mon2: Morning, @. The river mist is perfect today, so I am sketching it before it fades.$h
dialogue.Tue2: Careful where you step. I left a bucket of blue paint on the path. Half of Pelican Town has blue shoes now.
dialogue.Wed2: Folks think painting is easy. Try sitting still for six hours while the light moves, then tell me it is easy.
dialogue.Thu2: I need to ask the Dryad about the forest greens. She knows every shade the trees have ever worn.
dialogue.Fri2: The Dye Trader came through with a crate of wild dyes. Very flamboyant fellow. I bought one bottle and he wanted my soul.
dialogue.Sat2: Would you like to see my sketchbook? Warning, the first twenty pages are all my cat's tail. I was very ambitious back then.
dialogue.Sun2: Sunday strolls are the best. I usually end up at the river with my feet in the water and a brush in my pocket.$h
dialogue.Mon4: You are one of the few who actually looks at my paintings instead of just saying nice things. I appreciate that more than you know.$h
dialogue.Tue4: I painted a small figure in the corner of my last canvas, down by the river. Did you notice? I hope that is not too strange.$l
dialogue.Wed4: The Mechanic keeps asking why I do not paint something useful, like a wall. I told her a wall is just a canvas that gave up.$h
dialogue.Thu4: Being alone with paint all day can get quiet. I am glad the valley has people in it now. Good company makes better color.$h
dialogue.Fri4: The Stylist says my hat is out of fashion. I told her a painter's hat is supposed to be covered in splatters. That is the whole point.$a
dialogue.Sat4: Want to know a secret? I still have the first picture I ever sold, hanging over my bed. It is a bit lopsided, but I love it.$s
dialogue.Sun4: I wish I could paint how the sun feels on my face on a day like today. Maybe that is why I keep walking outside, @.$h
dialogue.Mon6: Do you know why I came to this valley? Quiet, cheap rent and a view of the forest. Turns out the view is better with someone to share it.$h
dialogue.Tue6: The Angler keeps pestering me to paint his fish. He says a fish portrait is the only honest kind. I told him he has no patience for art.$h
dialogue.Wed6: I used to paint portraits for coin. Now I paint what I see. Sometimes I see you in the corner of the canvas, and I do not know why.$l
dialogue.Thu6: The saloon has the best light in town, but the Tavernkeep will not let me paint his bar. Rules, rules.$a
dialogue.Fri6: My brushes are my family, and every one has a name. You are not allowed to ask what the one with the bent handle is called.$h
dialogue.Sat6: I dreamed the whole valley was a painting, and every person in it was a color. You were a very bright shade of gold.$h
dialogue.Sun6: When I am nervous I paint with my left hand. Everything comes out shaky, which is somehow honest. Do not tell the Nurse.$s
dialogue.Mon8: I hardly ever show anyone my unfinished work. Yet here you are, seeing every crooked line. Thank you for being patient with me.$l
dialogue.Tue8: Some days the blank canvas scares me more than anything in the mines. But when I have you to talk to, it feels less empty.$s
dialogue.Wed8: I think I finally found the color I have been chasing. It is the color of your farm at sunset. I could not stop painting it all night.$l
dialogue.Thu8: I dream about the cave paintings I made when I was young. Rough, honest, and full of wanting. You would have liked them.$h
dialogue.Fri8: I have been thinking about the life I want. A quiet house, a studio with a big window, and someone to argue colors with. Hmm.$l
dialogue.Sat8: Do you ever worry about what the Skeletron business did to the town? Some of us are still shaking. But you make me feel steady.$s
dialogue.Sun8: I trust you more than my own palette. If you ever need someone to see the world the way I do, I am right here, @.$l
dialogue.danceRejection: Dance with you at the Flower Dance? I would love to, but we do not know each other well enough yet. Ask me again when we are closer.$s
dialogue.spring_Wed: Spring paints itself. All I do is hold the brush and hope I do not ruin it.$h
dialogue.summer_Fri: Summer heat dries my paint in seconds. I have learned to work in the shade and cry a little less.$s
dialogue.fall_Sat: Fall is my favorite palette. Every maple and aspen is a new color to steal from.$h
dialogue.winter_Mon: Winter is quiet for painting. Snow turns the forest into one white page, and I hate to put a single mark on it.$h
dialogue.spring_15: The petals are falling early this year. I caught one on my brush and nearly cried.$s
dialogue.fall_20: Fallen leaves are the best free paint in the valley. I have a whole bag of them drying in my studio.$h
dialogue.summer_Tue: Summer nights are for painting the stars. My hand shakes less when I can see the sky.$h
dialogue.winter_Fri8: On a cold Friday you could sit in my studio and stay warm with me. Just think about it.$l

rainy: The rain is good for the forest but terrible for my easel. Every drop on a canvas is a little accident. I like the accidents best.$s

marriage.Indoor_Day_0: The light is good in here today, @. Stay and paint with me.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_1: Our little cottage smells of linseed oil and fresh bread. I would not trade it for anything.$h
marriage.Indoor_Day_2: I left my easel right in the doorway again. Sorry, love. Watch your step.$s
marriage.Indoor_Day_3: Come look at this sketch. It is you, asleep on the couch with your hat over your face. I could not resist.$l
marriage.Indoor_Day_4: Every corner of this house has a painting in it now. Most of them have you in them.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_0: Rain on the window and paint on my fingers. A perfect quiet day, @.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_1: I cannot paint outside in this rain, so I am painting the rain instead. Look how the drops fall.$h
marriage.Rainy_Day_2: The roof leaks over the studio again. I put a bucket under it, and the bucket is my new muse.$s
marriage.Rainy_Day_3: Sit with me by the window. The forest looks like a watercolor when it rains. I want you to see it.$l
marriage.Rainy_Day_4: Thank you for every rainy afternoon we have shared. They are my favorite days now.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_0: The candles are low tonight. I am glad you are home, @.$h
marriage.Indoor_Night_1: Turn the lamp down a little. The moon through the window is better than any paint I own.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_2: Did I snore in my sleep last night? Do not write it down in your notebook.$a
marriage.Indoor_Night_3: Come to bed, @. The canvas can wait until morning, I promise.$l
marriage.Indoor_Night_4: I used to paint alone at night. Now I hear your breathing and I know I am home.$l
marriage.Rainy_Night_0: The rain on the roof is so loud tonight. Hold my hand until it quiets down, please.$s
marriage.Rainy_Night_1: Storms make me restless. Stay awake with me a while and tell me the day's gossip.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_2: Do not let the thunder wake you. The Wizard says it is only the sky clearing its throat.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_3: If this rain keeps up, I will paint the storm on our bedroom wall. It will be dramatic.$h
marriage.Rainy_Night_4: Rainy nights with you beside me. I could not ask for a more perfect painting.$l
marriage.Outdoor_0: Let us take the easels out to the river. It is a beautiful evening for a walk, @.$h
marriage.Outdoor_1: The forest is glowing with sunlight. Hold my sketchbook while I try to catch it.$h
marriage.Outdoor_2: Careful on the bank, the mud is slippery. Give me your hand, love.$h
marriage.Outdoor_3: Look how the water shines. Every ripple is a brushstroke that nature painted all on its own.$h
marriage.Outdoor_4: Our walk always ends at this bend in the river. One day I will paint it, with us in it.$l
marriage.Good_0: Wonderful morning, @. I feel like I could paint the whole valley today.$h
marriage.Good_1: You always know when I need coffee. Thank you, dear.$h
marriage.Good_2: I was thinking about the old days, and I am glad they led me here to you.$h
marriage.Good_3: The Angler sent another request for a fish portrait. I laughed for an hour. Thank you for making my days lighter.$h
marriage.Good_4: Our little life is a good one, @. Simple, bright and full of color.$h
marriage.Good_5: I sold a painting to the Merchant today. He cheated me, but at least I had you to complain to afterward.$h
marriage.Good_6: Do you smell that? Someone is baking bread at the saloon. Let us go see who it is.$h
marriage.Good_7: You are the best model I have ever had, even when you fall asleep in the chair.$h
marriage.Good_8: I finished a painting of the farm at sunrise. It is my favorite, and you are standing in the front.$l
marriage.Good_9: I could sit like this forever, quiet and warm with you. Good day, @.$h
marriage.Neutral_0: Hm. Morning. My brushes are not cooperating today.$u
marriage.Neutral_1: Can you hand me the blue? No, the other blue. The one that is not sad.$u
marriage.Neutral_2: I have been staring at this canvas for an hour and it stares right back. Let us both lose.$u
marriage.Neutral_3: Not now, @, I am in the middle of a stroke. Come back in a bit.$a
marriage.Neutral_4: Oh, you are home. Good. Please take those boots off before you step on my drying paint.$a
marriage.Neutral_5: I think I need some quiet. Just for an afternoon, if that is all right.$s
marriage.Neutral_6: The Clothier is in the living room telling his cursed stories again. I need a break from him, and from my own mess.$a
marriage.Neutral_7: I was not asleep. I was thinking very hard with my eyes closed. That is what artists do.$u
marriage.Neutral_8: Sorry I snapped earlier. Painting makes me short-tempered, and you were just standing there looking handsome.$s
marriage.Neutral_9: Let's not talk about the grain bill. I am not in the mood for numbers today.$s
marriage.Bad_0: Please, not now. My brushes are dry and so is my patience.$a
marriage.Bad_1: The Mechanic borrowed my good easel and broke a leg off it. I am still furious.$a
marriage.Bad_2: You tracked mud through the studio again. I will be finding that mud for years.$a
marriage.Bad_3: Leave the canvases alone. They are fragile, and so am I today.$s
marriage.Bad_4: I am not sulking. I am sketching my disappointment in a very small corner.$a
marriage.Bad_5: Do not look at me like that. I know the frame is crooked. I know.$a
marriage.Bad_6: I have a headache from the turpentine and the Nurse says it is all my fault.$a
marriage.Bad_7: Go check on the Party Girl or something. My quiet time gets very loud when you stay.$a
marriage.Bad_8: I am sorry. Today's sadness is not your doing, but you do get the blame for standing near it.$s
marriage.Bad_9: Tomorrow we will be better, I promise. Just let me scrub the paint off my hands in peace.$s
marriage.OneKid_0: Our little one has smeared paint all over the kitchen wall. I think it is a masterpiece. Do not tell them that yet.$h
marriage.OneKid_1: The baby slept in my lap while I painted. Best model I have ever had, honestly.$l
marriage.OneKid_2: Look at the drawing our child made. It is a dog. Or a tree. Either way it is beautiful.$h
marriage.OneKid_3: Let the little one hold the brush for a minute. I know it is messy. That is how every painter starts.$h
marriage.TwoKids_0: Two little artists and a house full of paint. I would not change a single drop of it, @.$h
marriage.TwoKids_1: Both of them tried to paint the cat. The cat is not impressed, and neither am I, but I love them.$h
marriage.TwoKids_2: I promised the kids a picture each. Now I am behind on everything. Help me.$s
marriage.TwoKids_3: Look how the two of them chase the sunlight across the floor. I want to paint that exact moment.$l
marriage.NoBed_0: We have no bed in the studio yet. I sleep on the drop cloth and you get the chair. Fair?$u
marriage.NoBed_1: The bed is still in pieces from the move. I am sleeping on the sofa, so do not even ask.$s
marriage.NoBed_2: I do not mind the floor. Some of my best painting came from lying on wooden boards, staring at the stars.$h
marriage.NoBed_3: We will get a proper bed soon, I promise. Until then, my drop cloth is very comfortable.$h
marriage.patio_Leah: Let us sit on the patio with our tea and watch the forest. Nothing is more beautiful than this, @.$h
marriage.spouseRoom_Leah: I moved my easel into our room so I can paint you while you sleep. Do not complain, it is for art.$l
marriage.funLeave_Leah: I am off to the Mountain to sketch the Dryad's trees. Be good, and do not paint on the walls while I am gone.$h
marriage.funReturn_Leah: I am home! The Dryad let me paint her in her tent. She said I should marry a better painter. I said I already did.$l
marriage.Outdoor_Leah: The grass is soft today and the sun is warm. I could lie here with you all afternoon, @.$h
marriage.spring_Leah: Spring brings the best flowers for my palette. I have already found three new shades in the meadow.$h
marriage.summer_Leah: Summer evenings are for the river, my easel and you. Nothing else needs painting.$h
marriage.fall_Leah: Fall is when the forest looks like it is on fire. I want to paint all of it, with you beside me.$h
marriage.winter_Leah: Winter makes everything white and quiet. I am glad we are here together, warm by the fire.$l

situations.eye: Did you see that giant eye in the sky before you put it down? Nothing has ever looked at me so hard. I sketched it twice and burned both drawings.$u
situations.evilBoss: That corrupted thing from the deep is gone. My sketchbook is full of tentacles and I am not drawing them again.$s
situations.skeletron: The old dungeon is open and the Old Man is free. I painted him once, years ago, with a very sad face. Now I understand why.$s
situations.queenBee: The Queen Bee is no more, and the smell of honey hangs over the fields. Half my paints are sticky now. Worth it.$h
situations.hardmode: The Wall of Flesh has fallen and everything has turned strange, with bright new crystals on the hills. I am painting like mad before the Hallow swallows the view.$u
situations.mechs: One of those mechanical monsters was destroyed last night. The noise shook my canvases right off the wall. Good riddance.$a
situations.plantera: Plantera is defeated, so the jungle temple is open. The flowers there are the most magnificent colors I have ever seen. I need to go.$u
situations.golem: The Golem is finally smashed. Its stone face looked more like a painting than a monster, honestly.$h
situations.cultist: The Lunatic Cultist is defeated and the celestial pillars glow in the sky. I have never seen a sky so bright. I cried a little.$l
situations.moonLord: The Moon Lord is gone. The night sky looks cleaner now. I will paint it that way, with one bright star where he used to be.$h
situations.goblins: The goblin army came marching through and got chased off. I was too busy hiding behind my easel to help, sadly.$s
situations.pirates: The pirates were driven off last night. They knocked over my easel and stole a sunflower painting. Please help me get it back.$a
situations.frostLegion: The Frost Legion was pushed back north. Snow everywhere, and my paint froze in the tubes. Such a terrible mess.$s
situations.martians: The Martian Madness has ended. Strange beams and saucers in the sky, and every one looked like a bad drawing. I want to forget them.$u
situations.bloodMoon: The moon went red last night. I could not sleep, so I painted the forest in crimson until dawn. Strange work, but the night asked for it.$u
situations.eclipse: The sun went dark in the middle of the day. I stood outside with a jar of paint, staring. The sky painted itself that afternoon.$u
situations.party: The Party Girl is throwing a party today and asked me to paint the banners. I said yes, but only because the paint is free.$h

festivals.spring13: The Egg Festival! I am painting eggs with patterns nobody has seen before. Come see my table and bring a basket.$h
festivals.spring24: The Flower Dance. I wear my paint-stained smock and call it formal. Do not laugh at me, @.$h
festivals.summer11: The Luau! I put my sweet pepper stew into the community soup. It is the last thing I should have cooked. Taste carefully.$h
festivals.summer28: The Dance of the Moonlight Jellies. They glow in the water like living paint. I could watch them forever.$l
festivals.fall16: The Stardew Valley Fair. My painting of the grange hangs next to the pumpkins. Wish me luck with the judges.$h
festivals.fall27: Spirit's Eve. The haunted maze is spooky, but I painted every mural in it, and they are very cheerful for ghosts.$h
festivals.winter8: The Festival of Ice. I carved a snow sculpture shaped like a paint palette. It melted halfway through, which is somehow fitting.$u
festivals.winter25: The Feast of the Winter Star. I drew my gift tag myself and I hope it is the one you get. No peeking.$h
festivals.spring13_spouse: Our first Egg Festival as a married couple. I painted an egg just for you, shaped like a heart. Do not tell anyone.$l
festivals.spring24_spouse: The Flower Dance, and you are my partner. I will dance with you and only step on your feet a little.$l
festivals.summer11_spouse: I wrote our names on the community soup pot as a joke. Everyone laughed. I did not. I was blushing.$l
festivals.summer28_spouse: The jellies are glowing and you are holding my hand in the sand. This is the painting I always wanted to make.$l
festivals.fall16_spouse: Our painting won a ribbon at the Fair, and the judges called it lovely. I am so proud of us.$h
festivals.fall27_spouse: Spirit's Eve with you by my side. Even the ghosts look cheerful when you are around, @.$h
festivals.winter8_spouse: The ice sculptures are beautiful, but the one of you is the best. It is still melting, unfortunately.$l
festivals.winter25_spouse: I wrapped your gift in a little painting of us. It is the only gift I have ever made with my whole heart.$l

loved.text: A Paintbrush and a dye? @, you truly understand an artist.$l

liked.text: Lovely. Fresh flowers always find their way onto my canvas. Thank you.$h

neutral.text: Hm. Thank you, I suppose. Could I paint with this?

disliked.text: Ugh, trash. Do I look like a raccoon to you?$a

hated.text: Explosives near my easel? Are you trying to blow up the whole valley? Get that away from me.$a

events.after: Keep that spare brush clean or I will know about it.$h

steps.say: Oh! @, you startled me. Stand still, the light is perfect and I am about to lose it.$u
I am painting the river from memory. It changes every time I blink, so my memory has to work very hard.$h

answers.reply: Then come closer. Be honest, the frog in the corner is my favorite part.$h
A smudge? Then the smudge and I are both offended.$a

steps.say: Here, take this spare brush. Every painter needs one, and I have far too many.$h
There, now you can see my brushwork. Look at the little splash of gold on the water.$h

events.after: The Merchant has been watching me paint. I think he wants to buy the sky.$h

steps.say: Hold still, @, I am sketching the square. The fountain is hard to get right, the water never stops moving.$h
My very first painting was of this square. I sold it to the Merchant for two gold. He still brags about the bargain.$h

steps.question: Do you ever feel out of place here?

answers.reply: You say that like you mean it. I think I believe you.$l
Me too. Being new is lonely, but this town is kind when you let it be.$h

steps.say: Thank you for listening. Here, look, I drew you in the corner again.$l
Now go on before the sun moves. The light is already leaving.$h

events.after: The Dryad says I may paint her trees, so long as I keep my easel out of the roots.$h

steps.say: Ah, @. I came to paint the old oaks, but the Dryad was already here, glaring at my easel.$u
Painter, your colors are loud. The trees have opinions about them.
Ha! She has not warmed up to me yet, but I am working on her. Painting is all patience.$h

steps.question: Do you think she likes me?

answers.reply: Impressed? From a tree? That is practically a love letter.$l
Grumpy is just what she calls being careful.$h

steps.say: Thank you, old one. I will paint you properly, I swear it.$h
Walk back to town with me? I have a feeling the wind is about to turn cold.$h

events.after: Your portrait is not finished. Come back tomorrow and let me fix that hat.$l

steps.say: @, you came in so late. I left the lamp on for you, and the easel too, because I was painting you.$l
Look. It is you, standing by the river with the moon on your hat. I have never painted anyone like this before.$l

answers.text: I love it. It is perfect.
answers.reply: Then I will hang it right over the bed, where I can see it every night.$l
Silly? That hat is the most romantic thing in the valley.$a

steps.say: Stay a little longer. The candle is warm and the house is quiet.$l
Good night, @. Come back to me tomorrow, I am not finished with your portrait.$h

events.after: Light the way home with those glowsticks, and come find me tomorrow.$h

steps.say: The stars are out, @. I brought a lantern and a few glowsticks for the walk home.$l
The old sailors name stars after the people they love. I am choosing one for you.$l

answers.text: The brightest one over the sea.
answers.reply: The brightest one. You have good taste in stars, @.$l

answers.text: The little one that is hard to see.
answers.reply: Hard to see, yes. Still shining, and I would find it every night.$h

steps.say: Hold my hand, the sand is cold tonight.$l

events.after: Our portrait is hanging above the fireplace now. Look at all those colors, @.$l

steps.say: @, I finished the portrait. The two of us by the river in the first light of morning. Come look.$l
When I first came to Pelican Town I was alone with my brushes. Now I have a home full of color and a partner to argue with about it.$l
Hang it above the fireplace? Yes, let us hang it there. Everyone who visits will know exactly who I married.$h
Thank you for every brush stroke of this life, @. I love you.$l
Now let me add one last thing to the painting. A tiny heart in the corner, where only you will find it.$h
